newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican calls for global ban on human cloning.
newsitem.headline: Vatican calls for global ban on human cloning.

text.p: The Vatican called on Wednesday for a worldwide ban on human cloning as it joined the debate unleashed by the creation of a cloned sheep by British scientists.
Moral theologian Gino Concetti, who is close to Pope John Paul, said the creation of human life outside marriage went against God's plan.
"A person has the right to be born in a human way and not in the laboratory," Concetti wrote in an editorial in L'Osservatore Romano, the Vatican's semi-official newspaper.

"It is to be strongly hoped that states...will immediately pass a law that bans the application of cloning on humans and that in the face of the pressures from possibilist currents they have the force to make no concessions," he wrote.
"Reason and humanity make this a pressing request," he said.

The cloning by scientists in Scotland of Dolly the sheep, the first animal to be successfully cloned from an adult cell, has spread alarm worldwide about the possibility that the same technique could be extended to humans.

U.S. President Bill Clinton has ordered an urgent inquiry into the ethics of cloning while Nobel peace prize winning scientist Joseph Rotblat has compared the breakthrough with the creation of the atom bomb.
The Roman Catholic Church opposes all forms of artificial human conception, including test-tube fertilisation and surrogate motherhood.

Monsignor Elio Sgreccia, director of the institute of bioethics at the Catholic University in Rome, also argued on Wednesday that animal experimentation was valid only under very precise circumstances.
"It is justified only when there are serious and important reasons for the benefit of humanity or also for the benefit of the animals themselves," Sgreccia told Vatican Radio.

"But it also has to be said...that we must respect animal species," he said. "Carrying out an experiment on an individual (animal) for a serious reason of scientific research must not alter an animal species."
